business_scope.primary_industry_name: Middle-Market Cross-Border Cross-Industry M&A Advisory Boutique

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – federal common law for matters in the federal sphere; Quebec private law is civil law and commercial/regulatory matters are governed by Quebec's statutes and civil law tradition
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)
Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) with numerous counterparties, including Argentina, China, and several EU member states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; related FinTRAC regulations and guidance; Quebec Register of Enterprises (Registraire des entreprises du Québec) filing requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of status / good standing for each corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution / written consent of the general partner authorizing formation of the Quebec limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for all beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the partnership interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in each beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Quebec notarial deed / executed declaration of legal publicity (déclaration d'immatriculation) for the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (notaire) or the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Quebec; no apostille required if issued directly in Quebec

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, Interpol notices, FinTRAC risk indicators, and a commercially reputable global PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is required for all clients and counterparties in an M&A advisory boutique, including source-of-funds verification, negative-media review, and ongoing transaction monitoring under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Services en ligne / Online Services portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), every enterprise name used in Quebec must be in French. A non-French name may be permitted only in conjunction with a French version or a French generic term. All declarations filed with the RQ must be prepared in French; names are transliterated into the Latin alphabet and must comply with Quebec's distinctive-name requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any word suggesting a bank, trust company, insurer, or deposit-taking business, such as 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance', 'financing', 'savings'
Any word suggesting the practice of law or notarial services, such as 'lawyer', 'attorney', 'notary', 'legal services'
Words implying government, sovereign, or royal status, such as 'Canada', 'Quebec', 'royal', 'government', 'federal', 'municipal'
Words included in a name identical to or confusingly similar to an existing legal person or enterprise in Quebec
Any token requiring prior approval from a regulatory or professional order, including terms suggesting regulated financial services or securities dealing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects a requested name, the applicant may file an administrative review request (demande de révision) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the refusal, attaching written arguments and an alternative distinctive French-language name. If the review is unsuccessful, an appeal may be taken before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) in accordance with its rules; the applicant should simultaneously propose a revised name to avoid project delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally acceptable for the registered address of a Quebec limited partnership if the address is genuine, visible, and capable of receiving service of process. For an M&A advisory boutique, a virtual office is permissible as the statutory registered office, but the firm must maintain substantive operational substance, including full-time professional staff and records, and any required regulatory licensing or FINTRAC AML program should have a physical or verifiable presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 20% annual probability of unannounced inspection; enhanced scrutiny likely if the partnership is registered as a securities dealer or alternative investment dealer, or if the general partner is a non-resident entity with minimal local substance.

Legal due diligence opinion and formation structuring memorandum for a cross-border middle-market M&A advisory boutique

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (Code civil du Québec), arts. 2186 and 2236–2272 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 3, 15, 19 and 21 (mandatory registration, declaration and publication); Regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises; Securities Act (Québec), CQLR c. V-1.1, s. 5, read with National Instrument 31-103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations, s. 8.6 (M&A adviser exemption).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises of Québec) – Direction de l'immatriculation des entreprises, online portal 'Espace de transaction'
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Statement of Registration) of a société en commandite filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or contributed capital for a société en commandite. Limited partners must actually perform their promised contributions in money or property (not services) under CCQ arts. 2247–2248. No escrow or trust account is required by law at formation; the partnership agreement and contribution schedules govern funding. Each limited partner's liability is limited to its contributed capital when the partner does not participate in control and the registration is opposable to third parties.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner approves the partnership agreement of the société en commandite intended for registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the capital subscriptions undertaken by the limited partners, as set forth in the contribution schedules, are accepted and recorded in the partnership's capital register; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and principal establishment in Québec are fixed at the address indicated in the declaration, and the general partner is authorized to complete all statutory filings; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the managing partner and the secretary-treasurer are appointed, each acting alone, with authority to execute declarations, open bank accounts and sign client engagement agreements; and RESOLVED FINALLY, that all acts executed before this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search, validation and reservation of the limited partnership designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name search and reservation service ('Espace de transaction' / clerc du Registraire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a pre-validation search against the register of enterprises to verify that the proposed designation is not prohibited, identical or misleading under ss. 4 and 5 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; confirm the mandatory legal-form suffix 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; if required, file a name reservation with the Registraire (valid 90 days) to lock the designation before the declaration; obtain the name search report for the professional file.
required_dossiers: REQ name search report or reservation receipt
List of proposed names in order of preference (at least 3)
Legal form specification (société en commandite / S.E.C.)
Identification of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed designation is refused as identical or confusing, submit an amended name or obtain written consent from the prior name holder; a formal refusal notice may be contested with the Registraire within 30 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, s. 7.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement and general partner authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Counsel of the general partner / notary – private deed sufficient; notarial act (acte notarié en minute) recommended for evidentiary authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written partnership agreement under CCQ arts. 2236–2272 providing the firm name, head office, contribution schedule of the limited partners, profit/loss allocations, management powers reserved to the general partner, and withdrawal/capital return rules; the corporate general partner must adopt authorizing resolutions; each limited partner executes the contribution schedule; retain originals for the REQ file and AML/KYC documentation; execute in French, the official language of legal persons operating in Québec, or provide a certified French version if drafted in English.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (convention de société en commandite)
Contribution and capital account schedules
Board resolutions of the corporate general partner authorizing the partnership
Identification documents of all partners (AML/KYC file)
French-language attestation under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ requests a copy of the partnership agreement or a certified excerpt, provide a sworn true-copy excerpt; if a signature is challenged, obtain a confirmatory signature page and re-file; if a partner refuses to execute, the declaration cannot be completed and the transaction structure must be revised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ensuring registration in good standing of the general partner (declarant)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online accounts of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the corporate general partner holds a valid NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) with an up-to-date declaration; if the general partner is not yet registered, file its own declaration of registration or updating declaration first, because the limited partnership declaration must state the NEQ and status of each general partner; update the general partner's statement of activities to include management consultancy and M&A advisory services (NAICS 523150 / ISIC 7020).
required_dossiers: REQ attestation d'immatriculation (register extract) of the general partner
Updated declaration of the general partner, if applicable
List of directors and place of business of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the general partner's registration is inactive or contains inaccurate statements, file the correcting 'déclaration de mise à jour' online and wait for the revised REQ attestation before filing the LP declaration; if the general partner is a non-Canadian entity, appoint a mandatary for service of process in Québec and register that mandate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration of the limited partnership (immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – 'Espace de transaction' online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite: legal form, designation with 'S.E.C.' or 'société en commandite', principal establishment in Québec, head office, NEQ and name of each general partner, business activity (NAICS 523150 / ISIC 7020), number of establishments, and contact information; sign electronically as the authorized declarant; pay the statutory registration and publication fee (approximately CAD 44); receive the NEQ and attestation d'immatriculation immediately upon processing.
required_dossiers: Duly completed declaration form (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
Executed partnership agreement (for the registration file, produced on request)
NEQ and register status of the general partner
Proof of the principal establishment (lease, deed or landlord attestation)
Power of attorney or clerc authorization, if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon an information demand or notice of refusal from the REQ, file the missing documents within 15 days through the secure messaging of the Espace de transaction; if an omission is made within the first year, apply for a free correction; if the registration becomes overdue, the enterprise must cease activities until the regularization declaration is filed, with possible late-fee exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with Revenu Québec and AMF regulatory confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec – 'Inscription' portal; Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – registrations and exemptions office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the newly issued NEQ to activate the Revenu Québec file; register for QST (Québec sales tax) and GST/HST where taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or for voluntary registration; open source-deduction and payroll accounts if the partnership will employ personnel; submit a written opinion request to the AMF confirming that the M&A advisory activities qualify for the M&A adviser exemption under NI 31-103 s. 8.6 and therefore do not require dealer registration; if the boutique later facilitates securities distributions or runs a matching mandate, file for registration as an exempt market dealer under the Securities Act.
required_dossiers: NEQ and attestation d'immatriculation of the limited partnership
Exemption analysis memorandum under NI 31-103 s. 8.6
Partnership agreement and contribution schedules
Financial plan and fee model (success-fee wire and SWIFT rails)
AML/ATF compliance program documentation, if EMD registration becomes applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec assigns a different effective registration date or refuses voluntary QST opening, file a formal online 'demande de modification' with supporting invoices; if the AMF determines that the activities exceed the s. 8.6 exemption, file a registration application within the prescribed delay or restructure the mandate to avoid securities-related advice to third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, fire-safety, occupational-health and physical premises clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal building and fire safety service; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ); CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the office lease in the partnership's name; obtain from the landlord the building's occupancy certificate and fire-safety compliance attestation; request a municipal inspection for the 'certificat de sécurité incendie'; for any fit-out, confirm that the general contractor holds a valid RBQ licence and obtain a municipal renovation permit; file the CNESST Declaration of Establishment within the mandatory delay after the first hiring and post the required prevention notices; if a confidential records vault is installed, provide a structural load statement certified by an engineer; complete the final inspection and archive all clearances in the partnership compliance register.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease signed by the general partner
Certificate of occupancy of the building and municipal permit files
Fire-safety inspection request and resulting certificate
RBQ contractor licence evidence for the fit-out contractor
CNESST Declaration of Establishment and attestations
Structural load letter from an engineer, if a heavy records vault is installed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection lists deficiencies, submit a corrective compliance plan and request reinspection within 15 days; if the premises lack a certificate of occupancy, require the landlord to file a municipal regularization application and escalate to the permits office; if CNESST returns the establishment declaration, correct the risk class and re-file online, requesting waiver of late penalties where the original deadline was missed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – securities registration and exemptions; Registraire des entreprises du Québec – enterprise registration certificate; Revenu Québec – tax and sectoral registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Attestation d'immatriculation (Enterprise Registration Certificate) of the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, accompanied by an AMF conformity opinion confirming reliance on the M&A adviser exemption under NI 31-103 s. 8.6; no separate sectoral operating permit is required for a pure advisory boutique, but an Exempt Market Dealer licence under the AMF would become mandatory if the boutique engages in securities distribution or discretionary portfolio management.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'C' – Declarative-exempt: leasing and fit-out of an existing office unit below 500 m² in a multi-tenant commercial building is not listed among the mandatory EIA projects under the Règlement relatif à l'évaluation et l'examen des impacts sur l'environnement de certains projets (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23); a full environmental impact assessment is not required unless the fit-out involves new construction above 500 m², sensitive watercourse work, or a major transformation of the building envelope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office occupancy generates no process wastewater; sanitary effluents must meet municipal sewer by-laws and the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'eau (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 18) through the city treatment plant. Air emissions are limited to negligible VOCs from office operations; HVAC refrigerants must be managed under the Règlement sur les halocarbures (CQLR c. E-12.1, r. 3); residual waste sorting and recycling must comply with municipal by-laws and, where applicable, the redevance regime for residual material disposal. No industrial discharge permits apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the local fire prevention service following an inspection under the Building Act and the Code de sécurité du Québec; building occupancy certificate validated for the 'Bureau' assembly category; structural load verification of any confidential records vault; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) contractor licence evidence for tenant fit-out works; CNESST occupational health clearance through the Declaration of Establishment under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1, s. 62, together with the posting of the workplace prevention program and first-aid attestations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and CRA My Business Account, for the federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST program account, non-resident income-tax filings, information returns, and partnership reporting. Revenu Québec, including its online services portal, administers Québec Sales Tax (QST), Québec income-tax matters, source deductions, and Québec partnership information obligations. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers import and export customs documentation and the Canada Border Services Agency CARM system for commercial importers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Québec limited partnership carrying on business or earning income in Canada should obtain a CRA nine-digit Business Number through Business Registration Online or the CRA non-resident registration process, using the partnership agreement, legal name, Québec registration or business-registration evidence where applicable, principal business activity, fiscal period, Canadian and foreign addresses, responsible partners, authorized representative, and ownership or control information. The partnership should open the applicable CRA program accounts, including GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP) if employees are present, and information-return accounts where required. A non-resident partnership should appoint an authorized representative or use a Canadian tax intermediary where operationally necessary and maintain evidence of Canadian business activity and its partnership status. Registration for GST/HST is made with the CRA; registration for QST is generally made separately with Revenu Québec. A non-resident partnership supplying taxable services in Québec must assess both GST/HST and QST registration obligations and whether it is carrying on business in Canada or Québec. Registration is not itself a substitute for any Québec enterprise-registration, professional-regulatory, securities, or financial-services licensing requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general US-style check-the-box election for a limited partnership. A valid Canadian partnership is generally fiscally transparent: the partnership computes income and allocates each partner's share under the Income Tax Act, while partners are generally taxed on allocated income. A partnership may elect or make statutory designations where specifically permitted, including elections or designations affecting partnership income allocations, dispositions of partnership interests, and certain transfers under the Income Tax Act; these are not entity-classification elections. Canadian anti-hybrid mismatch rules can deny deductions or impose inclusion where a foreign classification or instrument mismatch produces a deduction/non-inclusion or duplicate deduction outcome. The legal characterization of a foreign or Canadian LP must be supported by its agreement, governing law, conduct, and tax attributes; a foreign jurisdiction's entity election does not automatically bind Canada or Québec.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Harmonized Sales Tax (HST), administered by the CRA, together with Québec Sales Tax (QST), administered by Revenu Québec. Québec generally applies GST at the federal level and QST at the provincial level rather than HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, calculated under the small-supplier rules, generally triggers GST/HST registration when exceeded in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Québec generally uses a CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST registration, subject to the detailed QST rules and exceptions. Voluntary registration may be available below the threshold. The 5.0% headline rate is the federal GST rate; Québec QST is generally 9.975%, and the combined ordinary Québec consumption-tax burden is generally 14.975%. Special rules apply to financial services, specified listed financial institutions, real property, imported taxable supplies, digital-economy supplies, and supplies made through platforms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not generally require real-time electronic invoice clearance, mandatory government pre-approval, or universal fiscal digital stamping for ordinary M&A advisory invoices. A GST/HST or QST registrant must issue compliant invoices or other prescribed records, retain source documents and electronic books, and provide sufficient information for tax identification, consideration, tax rate, tax amount, place-of-supply analysis, and input-tax-credit or input-tax-refund support. Electronic records are acceptable if they remain accessible, reliable, readable, and capable of audit reproduction. CRA electronic filing is required for many GST/HST registrants, including registrants subject to mandatory electronic-filing rules, and Revenu Québec may impose electronic filing requirements for QST returns or specified registrants. Electronic funds transfer, payment-processor, and platform records should be reconciled to invoices, contracts, engagement letters, and bank receipts. There is no general Canadian or Québec requirement to transmit every invoice through a government clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, GST/HST and QST zero-rating generally requires that the goods be exported from Canada or Québec in circumstances satisfying the applicable place-of-supply and documentary conditions; the supplier must retain evidence of export, purchaser identity, delivery terms, carrier movement, customs reporting, and destination outside Canada. For M&A advisory and other professional services, a supply to a non-resident may be zero-rated where the recipient is not resident in Canada and the service is not excluded by the statutory rules, including rules for services in respect of real property or tangible personal property in Canada, litigation or dispute-related services concerning Canadian proceedings, services performed in Canada in certain circumstances, and supplies made to an individual in Canada. The supplier must verify the customer's non-resident status, obtain contractual and commercial-use evidence, identify the actual recipient and beneficiary, document where the services are performed and used, and analyze whether the service is connected with Canadian securities, financial instruments, Canadian real property, or another excluded category. Zero-rating is not available merely because the client pays from offshore or the transaction is cross-border. Exported services must be distinguished from exempt financial services, which generally do not carry GST/HST or QST and generally do not generate input-tax-credit or input-tax-refund entitlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or applicable CBSA export-reporting record, where required
Commercial invoice, engagement or supply contract, purchase order, and written description of the exported goods or services
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, courier manifest, or other carrier evidence showing movement of goods outside Canada
Proof of delivery or foreign receipt and destination-country import or customs record, where applicable
Recipient's foreign legal name, address, tax-registration details where available, and evidence that the recipient is non-resident for GST/HST and QST purposes

For exported advisory services, engagement letter, deliverables, time records, correspondence, transaction-closing records, evidence of service location and use, and analysis supporting the zero-rating provision
Bank statement, wire confirmation, SWIFT message, or other payment evidence linking consideration to the invoice; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a general Canadian statutory document
GST/HST and QST invoices or equivalent prescribed records showing the applicable zero-rated treatment and tax amount of zero
Foreign exchange conversion records and general-ledger reconciliation where consideration is received in a foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: Not applicable. Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds or service fees be repatriated within 180 days. Foreign-exchange controls do not generally impose a fixed repatriation deadline, although anti-money-laundering, customs, transfer-pricing, tax-record retention, foreign-reporting, sanctions, and financial-institution documentation rules may apply. Any contractual, banking, grant, or foreign-jurisdiction repatriation condition must be analyzed separately.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess tax, deny zero-rating, deny input tax credits or input tax refunds, and assess the unpaid GST/HST or QST retroactively, generally together with arrears interest and applicable penalties. A supplier that incorrectly treats a taxable domestic supply as zero-rated can become liable for the uncollected tax, subject to statutory purchaser-relief and assessment rules. Penalties may include failure-to-file, failure-to-remit, repeated-failure, gross-negligence, false-statement, and false-return penalties; gross-negligence penalties can generally be 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, while tax-evasion conduct may result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Customs misdeclarations may attract CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System sanctions, seizure, forfeiture, reassessment of duties and taxes, and prosecution. Québec may impose separate QST interest and penalties. Fraudulent or unsupported export claims should be corrected through amended returns, repayment of improperly claimed refunds or credits, and preservation of the full audit trail; limitation periods can be extended or eliminated in cases involving misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful blindness, or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; Canada maintains no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration, as the statutory exchange-control regime was repealed in 1958. Cross-border fund surveillance and anti-money-laundering/anti-terrorist-financing oversight of transfer flows are administered by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Prudential supervision of deposit-taking, escrow, and FX dealing institutions is performed by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); Quebec-specific money-services-business licensing is administered by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Act respecting money-services businesses (CQLR c E-12.000001).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and maintains full convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no statutory restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or repatriation of partnership capital from a Quebec limited partnership; the Canadian dollar is freely floating and fully transferable. Practical frictions are limited to: (i) mandatory FINTRAC reporting of cross-border electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; (ii) Part XIII or Quebec withholding tax on distributions to non-resident limited partners, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty; (iii) Investment Canada Act review, which is confined to foreign acquisitions of control of Canadian businesses and does not impede outbound advisory fee flows; and (iv) Canadian economic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, which may block transactions involving designated jurisdictions or persons. For the M&A advisory boutique, success fees in USD/EUR are receivable offshore without limitation, and no central-bank approval is required for any conversion or remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion regime. The former Exchange Control Act requirements were abolished in 1958, and neither exporters nor cross-border service providers such as M&A advisors are required to convert foreign-currency earnings into Canadian dollars within any statutory timeline or ratio. The limited partnership may retain 100% of cross-border success fees in USD/EUR accounts at Schedule I banks or convert them at its sole discretion. The only compliance obligations are transactional: FINTRAC cross-border currency and EFT reports for physical or electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and consistent recording of foreign-currency receipts in the LP capital accounts for Canadian and Quebec income tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM (conditional / ancillary use only). Legal constraints: (i) any non-resident electronic-money institution (EMI) operating in Canada as a money-services business must register with FINTRAC as an MSB under the PCMLTFA and, if active in Quebec, obtain an AMF permit under the Act respecting money-services businesses; (ii) foreign digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or US-licensed platforms may be used by the LP solely as payment-collection agents for small advisory retainers, not as custodians of client escrow or settlement funds, because they lack CAD clearing through LVTS/Real-Time Rail and cannot provide documentary credit or secured escrow; (iii) the LP must disclose any EMI relationship to its primary banks and include aggregated EMI transfers in FINTRAC EFT reports once the CAD 10,000 threshold is crossed; (iv) reliance on foreign EMIs for material success-fee flows is incompatible with the statutory escrow and trust-account expectations of Canadian M&A counterparties and creates an adverse client-acceptance profile for the boutique.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated under PCMLTFA, but in practice Schedule I banks impose an enhanced due-diligence interview for a 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' M&A advisory LP. One in-branch or FINTRAC-compliant videoconference KYC interview is required with the general partner and the lead beneficial owner. Upon completion of the videoconference interview, remote account opening is attainable at National Bank of Canada and RBC for Canadian-resident principals. Mandatory documentary kit: (i) notarized/certified extract of the LP declaration of registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ); (ii) executed partnership agreement and GP resolution; (iii) UBO confirmation to the 25% ownership threshold, including identification of all non-resident limited partners; (iv) certified passports/driver licenses of the GP directors and any 25%-or-more partners; (v) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; and (vi) commercial references, normally from the principal advisors/legal counsel or a prior tier-one banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the UBO chain: non-resident limited partners, nominee partners, or trust-held LP interests obscuring ownership beyond 25% threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certified partnership register extract (NEQ); full UBO organizational chart to each 25%+ owner; sworn statutory declarations from every limited partner; certified passports and proof of address; detailed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements covering each material contributor; independent corporate or banking reference for any non-resident LP; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for each ownership layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty or jurisdiction exposure: M&A targets, buyers, or fee payors located in sanctioned or enhanced-risk states, or transaction value near FINTRAC reporting thresholds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Positive sanctions screening results against Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU/UK United Nations lists; negative-media and adverse-information search report; transaction rationale and economic-substance memorandum; copy of the engagement letter identifying the ultimate fee payor; contractual sanctions and anti-money-laundering undertakings from the counterparty; and an enhanced transaction-monitoring protocol approved by the LP's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum success-fee wire inflow presenting a potential structuring or money-laundering typology
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed engagement letter with itemized fee formula; closing or milestone-completion certificate signed by both the client and the LP; final success-fee invoice; general-partner resolution approving receipt and allocation of the fee; third-party escrow closing statement; underlying transaction evidence (executed purchase agreement, closing press release, or securities-commission filing); pre-notification to the receiving bank for any inbound wire above USD/CAD 100,000, accompanied by this dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Excessive use of intermediary banks, multi-hop cross-border routing, or third-party payments creating clearing opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cleared-funds routing memorandum identifying the payer and beneficiary name-match with the contractual counterpart; documented commercial justification for each intermediary bank; FX conversion confirmation from the executing bank; periodic counterparty reconciliation schedule; standing instruction prohibiting payments from unrelated third parties; and a board-approved policy excluding walk-in cash, bearer instruments, or virtual-asset transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office-only presence or virtual-office red flag suggesting the absence of substantive operations in Quebec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed office lease or serviced-office agreement for Quebec premises; NEQ registry proof of active status; applicable business license; corporate telephone and email domain records; payroll and business-expense records evidencing operational substance; presence declaration from the general partner and principal deal team; and, if remote, a documented supervision protocol showing the location of books, records, and signatories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for partner capital contributions and equity injections: (i) the payer originates a SWIFT MT103 to the LP's collection account at a Schedule I bank, using the bank's BIC, Canadian clearing code (3-digit institution number plus 5-digit transit), and the LP's beneficiary account number; (ii) the payment narrative or purpose code must read 'LP capital contribution / subscription' or 'Investment – advisory equity', and must reference the executed subscription agreement and the LP capital-account identifier; (iii) where the contribution is received in USD or EUR, the bank's treasury desk executes a same-day conversion to CAD at the relevant spot, or the conversion is pre-hedged under a forward; (iv) the receiving institution is obligated to file a FINTRAC EFT report for any cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; (v) internal verification requires the bank credit memorandum to be reconciled against the executed subscription agreement, the LP capital-account ledger, and a partner instruction letter; (vi) hardening controls: cash deposits exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable, bearer instruments and in-kind contributions are prohibited without an independent valuation, and no third-party nominee may inject capital without full UBO disclosure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail hierarchy for trade settlements and advisory disbursements: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments in USD/EUR, with field 70 narrative stating 'Success fee under engagement agreement dated [X]' and field 71A charged as 'OUR', settling same-day via Fedwire/CHIPS (USD) or TARGET2 (EUR); (ii) for domestic Canadian-dollar disbursements above CAD 25,000, use the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) providing real-time gross settlement finality; below that threshold, use standard EFT or the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for instant small-value payments; (iii) for deal-contingent payments to escrow agents, legal counsel, or counter parties requiring documentary security, use a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) issued or confirmed by a Schedule I Canadian bank, coupled with escrow release instructions authenticated by two approved signatories; (iv) every outbound disbursement is matched to an executed invoice and a general-partner resolution, with FINTRAC EFT reporting where the transaction reaches or exceeds CAD 10,000; (v) prohibited rails for the boutique: virtual-asset transfers, bearer checks, cash couriers, and any unlabelled third-party payment channels that would compromise the audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, executed bilaterally with a Schedule I bank under standard ISDA/CSA or master FX agreements, to hedge known success-fee receivables and foreign-currency operating costs.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market or restricted currencies (for example CLP, BRL, MXN, or ARS) where a cross-border M&A mandate involves target or buyer cash flows denominated in those currencies, with net settlement in CAD/USD through the bank's offshore FX desk.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY/CCS) aligned with deferred earn-out receivables or vendor-note liabilities in foreign currencies, fixing the LP's combined FX and interest-rate exposure under ISDA 2002 with CSA credit support.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the registered limited partnership (société en commandite)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Registre des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of the partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative fines under the Act respecting legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (CQLR c P-45); continued default for over 12 months may lead to administrative strike-off, cancellation of the registration, and loss of limited-partner protection against third-party claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) with partner allocation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the fifth month following the partnership's fiscal period-end; for a December 31 year-end the filing deadline is May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under section 162 of the Income Tax Act (CAD 10 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 5,000); intentional omission or false reporting may additionally attract gross-negligence penalties, interest, and partner-level reassessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec limited partnerships are not automatically subject to a statutory independent audit. An audit becomes compulsory where the partnership agreement requires it, where the entity holds an Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) registration such as an exempt market dealer or M&A advisory authorization, where the partnership qualifies as a publicly accountable enterprise, or where a lender or investor imposes an audit covenant. For this cross-border M&A advisory boutique, audited annual financial statements will in practice be required by the AMF registration condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private limited partnerships may apply ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) or another agreed-upon basis of accounting permitted by the partnership agreement. Income tax reporting must separately comply with the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec) and must be reflected in the federal T5013 and applicable Quebec partner information schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships. The annual declaration to the REQ confirms the general partner, registered limited partners, and the establishment address; changes in limited partners are registered by way of an amendment filed within 30 days of the change. For the M&A advisory boutique, the FinTRAC compliance program must annually verify and document the beneficial ownership of the limited partnership itself and each engagement counterparty under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and the compliance officer must confirm that the register of limited partners is aligned with the latest share-transfer or interest-transfer records.
